name: Crackhead Control
description: Crackhead Control is a high rubber-guard clinch that reinforces Mission Control by bringing the second leg high behind the opponent's head, helping retain posture control while the arms remain inside.
summary: Crackhead Control is a high rubber-guard clinch that reinforces Mission Control by bringing the second leg high behind the opponent's head, helping retain posture control while the arms remain inside.
overview:
The bottom player keeps the opponent close with a Mission Control leg and hand connection. The second leg rises high to reinforce the upper-body clinch behind the head. The opponent's arms remain inside and must still be managed before an arm-isolation attack. The bottom player adjusts from the hips while the top player works to recover posture and inside frames.

This is a facing guard configuration. Unlike the basic Invisible Collar path, it does not require first clearing an arm to the mat and clearing the neck; unlike Dead Orchard, it does not define a completed both-arm leg triangle. Terminology: Crackhead rubber-guard control.

Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle. Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.

The high clinch is optional: release if the knee is twisted, the neck is stacked, or either partner signals discomfort. Do not use high-leg closure as a neck crank.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 169: the Pump](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/techniques/mts-169-rubber-guard-the-pump/); [10th Planet Costa Mesa — basic path with double bagger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W2OFKidf9lE).
key_principles: Start with broken posture: Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg.
Bring the second leg high: Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
Track both elbows: Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.
Keep knees close: Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees.
Return to one-leg control: Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again.
Open against a stack: Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

flashcards.question: Crackhead defense: what arm habit avoids offering an easy isolation between the high legs?
flashcards.answer: Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep the elbows bent and close

plausible: Reach both arms straight toward the far hip
Post one hand far behind the opponent's head
trap: Lock the elbows to lift against the leg clinch

flashcards.question: Crackhead defense: what does a second leg rising behind your head add?
flashcards.answer: A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem.

plausible: An inside frame that lifts your head away from the first shin
A low hip clamp replacing the first leg behind your head
trap: A completed triangle isolating both shoulders

flashcards.question: Crackhead defense: before the upper clinch closes, where can you establish a useful early frame?
flashcards.answer: Build a balanced base and an early hip frame before the high clinch closes.
flashcards.answer_line: At the opponent's hip line with a balanced base

plausible: Behind their head with both elbows extended
On the mat beyond their far shoulder
trap: On the outside of the raised thigh with your elbow flared away

flashcards.question: Crackhead defense: what comes before standing tall or extracting an arm?
flashcards.answer: Undo the high-leg connection before attempting to stand tall or extract an arm.

plausible: Straighten the trapped elbow against their thigh
Lift the chin while both legs stay behind your head
trap: Turn your shoulders while the wrists remain fixed

flashcards.question: Crackhead defense: why is a forceful stack a poor answer to the high clinch?
flashcards.answer: Do not answer the clinch by driving the partner onto the neck.
flashcards.answer_line: It can compress the bottom player's neck without freeing you

plausible: Forward pressure slides the reinforcing leg below the shoulder
The neck fold draws both elbows back inside the high legs
trap: The bottom player must open the knee hug to support the stack

flashcards.question: Crackhead defense: when is ordinary guard passing a reasonable next phase?
flashcards.answer: Begin ordinary guard passing once the shoulders and arms are free of the high enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: After your shoulders and arms leave the high enclosure

plausible: As soon as one knee moves outside their lower hip
While the second leg still pins your head down
trap: Before addressing either high-leg connection

flashcards.question: Crackhead defense: which first control supports the opponent adding the second leg?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player keeps the opponent close with a Mission Control leg and hand connection.

plausible: A low ankle crossing with neither shin held behind the head
A high shin resting unsupported while both hands pull the wrists
trap: A knee shield between the chests with the foot at the hip

flashcards.question: Crackhead defense: why does a high two-leg clinch not necessarily mean Dead Orchard is complete?
flashcards.answer: This is a facing guard configuration. Unlike the basic Invisible Collar path, it does not require first clearing an arm to the mat and clearing the neck; unlike Dead Orchard, it does not define a completed both-arm leg triangle.
flashcards.answer_line: Both shoulders still need its specific closed leg triangle

plausible: The second foot behind the head is enough regardless of elbow position
The ankle crossing at the waist defines the two-arm trap
trap: A high shin and one overhook supply the same enclosure

bottom.overview:
The bottom player is responsible for maintaining the control. The bottom player keeps the opponent close with a Mission Control leg and hand connection. The second leg rises high to reinforce the upper-body clinch behind the head. The opponent's arms remain inside and must still be managed before an arm-isolation attack. flashcards.answer: Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Broken posture with the first leg supported by your hand

plausible: Upright opposing posture with the first knee below the shoulder
A loose first leg with both hands posted on the mat
trap: A wrist pull with the first shin slipping off the upper back

flashcards.question: Crackhead control: what is the purpose of bringing the second leg high?
flashcards.answer: Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
flashcards.answer_line: Reinforce the upper-body clinch behind the head

plausible: Replace the first leg with a low clamp around the waist
Complete a straight-arm lever without checking either elbow
trap: Put the shin beneath the chin while releasing the first knee hug

flashcards.question: Crackhead control: what must you keep checking before claiming an arm-isolation attack?
flashcards.answer: Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.
flashcards.answer_line: The position of both opposing elbows

plausible: Only whether your feet have joined behind the head
Only whether the second shin is higher than the first
trap: Only whether the opponent can lift the chin

flashcards.question: Crackhead control: how should you tighten the leg connection without levering your own knees?
flashcards.answer: Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees.
flashcards.answer_line: Adjust the hips and keep the knees close

plausible: Pull both feet inward against stationary knees
Flatten your hips and yank the ankles upward
trap: Push the knees wide while crossing the feet harder

flashcards.question: Crackhead control: how can you return to Mission Control?
flashcards.answer: Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again.
flashcards.answer_line: Lower the second leg while retaining the first shin grip

plausible: Release the first shin and keep only the second foot
Remove both hand grips before moving either leg
trap: Straighten both knees while keeping the ankles crossed

flashcards.question: Crackhead control: what should you do when the opponent compresses your upper back in a stack?
flashcards.answer: Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the clinch and rebuild frames

plausible: Pull both feet closer while your hips stay trapped
Hold the legs shut and extend both arms overhead
trap: Keep the neck loaded until an elbow becomes available

flashcards.question: Crackhead control: what keeps the opponent close while your free leg travels upward?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player keeps the opponent close with a Mission Control leg and hand connection.

The low leg pressing the hip while the first high knee drops away
trap: The rising foot alone before it has connected behind the head
